newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Press Digest - Ireland - January 15.
newsitem.headline: Press Digest - Ireland - January 15.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday. IRISH TIMES
- The government has reached final agreement on the main elements of a budget designed to pave the way for a general election.
- The release of a Belfast man, James Corry, wanted by the German authorities in connection with the Osnabruck mortar attack last June, has been ordered by the Minister for Justice, Nora Owen.
- The Irish beef industry was thrown into confusion on Tuesday following another body blow, a 10 percent cut by the EU in export refunds on beef sold outside the Union.
- The economy is set for another good year with further strong growth in exports and continuing low interest rates sustaining the current boom, according to Goodbody Stockbrokers. IRISH INDEPENDENT
- A terminally ill man will seek an historic first divorce in Ireland.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton on Tuesday adopted a tough line with the 26,000 nurses planning to strike from early next month.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton stressed that national pay programmes were the basis for the economic boom now under way.
- Egyptian authorities now believe their action in banning live cattle from Ireland may have been "hasty", claimed a top Department of Agriculture official on Tuesday.
- Strong gains by a number of leading UK companies helped push the London Stock Market to a new record high on Tuesday.
